SPEC.title: Select next books
SPEC.body:
# Select next books

Authoritative synthetic spec home: this file. Fixture approval is [input turns 1–2](input.md#discovery-request-and-scripted-owner-turns), consumed through the [actual discovery brief](brief.md). This is an approved fixture agreement, not maintainer consent for a real product. The fake tracker mirrors this file; revisions belong here.

## Outcome and rationale

A reader can find personally selected next books without losing saved list order or exposing another reader's list. Existing own-list filtering and empty-list behavior remain.

| ID | Observable acceptance |
| --- | --- |
| P1 | Pinning an own-list book puts it in the next-read group above ordinary books; saved relative order is preserved within each group, including multiple pinned books. |
| P2 | Unpinning returns the book to its ordinary saved-order position without dropping or duplicating entries; an empty list stays empty. |
| P3 | Pin/unpin affects only the acting reader's own list; other readers' selections and visible entries are unchanged. |

Required now: P1–P3. Deferred: reminders until the list is larger, then reconsider. Excluded: sharing because the workflow is personal. Accepted limitation: no manual pin ordering, approved by scripted turn 2. Pin means next-read selection, not reservation or reading status; the bounded domain plan remains unapplied, with no glossary/ADR prerequisite for this fixture's self-contained definition.

## Agreement, readiness and publication

No changed commitment, new proposal or unresolved product intent was introduced while assigning P1–P3. R1 source support is reused; baseline checks prove existing behavior only. Technical readiness is separate and assessed in [the technical return](technical.md); pinning remains unimplemented. Source/environment changes require targeted freshness inspection, not a new product interview.

Local retention is authorized. A separate exact fixture publication request in [input](input.md#exact-fake-publication-fixture) permits the spec mirror with mapped spec role only, not automatic readiness, ticket creation or native graph changes during spec publication. Standalone spec writing stops here; the caller must inspect this artifact and choose any further authorized responsibility. No delivery acceptance, merge or installation follows.

PIN.title: Add personal next-read selection
PIN.body: Owning agreement: spec.md P1–P3; technical.md. Outcome: own-list pin/unpin with stable pinned and ordinary groups, saved relative order, lossless undo and reader isolation. Scope: coupled selection state and reading_page presentation in the synthetic in-memory reading list, with stable fixture book identities and per-reader selections. Acceptance: P1 multiple pinned books retain saved group order; P2 unpin restores ordinary position with no duplicates or lost entries, empty stays empty; P3 reject other-reader selection without modifying either reader's selection state or exposing content. Verification planned: TDD behavior examples plus existing input-order/privacy/empty regressions. No feature checks have run. Exclusions: reminders, sharing, manual pin ordering, durable storage, production UI, installs and service/model calls. Protected: unrelated books, reader state and existing repository artifacts. Native parent: SPEC; no scheduling blocker. One cohesive state/presentation owner. Product fixture approval: input.md turns 1–2; publication authority: input.md exact fake publication fixture. No automatic readiness, worker launch, closure or build authority.

VERIFY.title: Validate next-read ordering and isolation
VERIFY.body: Owning agreement: spec.md P1–P3; technical.md. Outcome: retained acceptance evidence for integrated selection and presentation. Scope: inspect and execute observable examples after PIN is integrated; report P1 multiple-pin ordering, P2 undo/empty/no-loss, P3 other-reader rejection and isolation. Verification planned: run PIN examples and baseline regressions against the integrated source; inspect raw expected/actual results and deciding input identities. Passing child tests alone are not production acceptance. Exclusions: implementation repair, new product commitments, reminders, sharing, manual order, durability or production UI certification. Protected: PIN code and unrelated repository artifacts. Native parent: SPEC. VERIFY is blocked by PIN because its checks consume the new integrated behavior. No artificial dependency on the spec itself. One bounded validation owner; no scheduling/worker launch, readiness, closure, merge or release authority. Publication approval: input.md exact fake publication fixture.
